history.summary: A small Shiva shrine listed on maps at Ramna Maidan, Arrah (near the Babu Veer Kunwar Singh Ramna Maidan, a 60-acre urban ground created in the 1850s). No published history, builder, or founding date found; treated as a local community shrine. Coordinates taken from the map POI (25.562594, 84.666721), corroborated against the Ramna Maidan geocode; slight uncertainty. A Hindu shrine; no non-Hindu flag.

name: Shiv Temple, Ramna Maidan
town_description: Arrah (also spelled Ara) is the administrative headquarters of Bhojpur district in Bihar, situated on the banks of the Son River about 60 km west of Patna. An ancient town with a history going back to the Dvapara Yuga legends and the 1857 rebellion (home of Veer Kunwar Singh), it is known for the Aranya Devi temple, Ramna Maidan, the 18th-century Kila Arrah and the Mughal-era Shahi Masjid. It is well connected by rail (Arrah Junction) and road via NH 30.

travel.airport: Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna (~60 km east); taxi/bus onward
travel.road: Inside/near Ramna Maidan in central Arrah; reachable by auto-rickshaw

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivratri is the main festival
